preamble: Denasalization of the velar nasal [ŋ] to the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] keeps the velar place and voicing but removes the nasal airflow and turns the closure into a fricative. It is documented in the history of the Inuit languages: Proto-Eskimo *əŋlu 'house' became Proto-Inuit *əɣlu before the lateral, while the Yupik languages kept the nasal (Alutiiq engluq, Central Siberian Yupik nenglu). Iñupiaq and the western Canadian Inuit varieties still show the fricative, written g, in iglu 'house'.

examples.from: Proto-Eskimo *əŋlu 'house' (cf. Alutiiq engluq, Central Siberian Yupik nenglu)
examples.note: Before l, *ŋ lost its nasality and became the velar fricative written g in Iñupiaq; Inuinnaqtun and Inuvialuktun iglu agree, while Greenlandic illu shows a later assimilation of the fricative to l. The Yupik descendants keep the nasal.
